title: Reproducibility package: Temporal spinal transcriptomic reprogramming and stimulation-associated candidate genes in neuropathic pain
description:
Analysis scripts and intermediate result tables supporting a criterion-explicit cross-dataset re-analysis of four public spinal cord datasets.

Datasets. GSE175760 (rat chronic constriction injury, lumbar spinal cord, bulk RNA-seq, six groups × n = 3; discovery cohort), GSE5296 (mouse contusive spinal cord injury microarray, 96 samples; cross-platform direction concordance), GSE243038 (mouse spinal motoneurons, Smart-seq2; descriptive stimulation-associated trends), GSE189070 (mouse spinal cord single-cell RNA-seq; cell-type expression reference). All data were obtained from the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus; no new data were generated.

Contents. (i) R and Python scripts covering differential expression with limma-trend on the unified scale log2(FPKM + 0.1), fuzzy c-means temporal clustering, WGCNA, LASSO and SVM-RFE candidate prioritisation, GSVA with MSigDB Hallmark sets, PROGENy, functional enrichment, cross-platform concordance and cell-type annotation; (ii) the intermediate result tables from which every number in the manuscript is derived; (iii) the five main figures as 600 dpi PNG and vector PDF, and the two main tables.

Methodological notes. Two differential-expression thresholds are reported in parallel (strict: Benjamini–Hochberg FDR < 0.05 with |log2FC| > 0.58; exploratory: nominal P < 0.05 with |log2FC| > 0.58). The GSE5296 matrix as distributed is a linearised back-transformation of RMA log2 values and was log2-transformed before computation, with strain fitted as a covariate. The GSE243038 dataset was analysed descriptively only, without inferential statistics, because its three samples per condition correspond to three stimulation frequencies rather than biological replicates.

Scope. No wet-laboratory validation was performed. All statements in the associated manuscript are hypotheses or dataset descriptions.
